purpose: Resolve the integration boundary between Payload's auth-enabled Users collection and the canonical Session entity without inferring framework internals as application persistence evidence.
integrationRules: Payload auth-generated fields or session behavior MUST NOT be treated as canonical ENT-SESSION persistence evidence unless the concrete schema and runtime behavior are inspected and mapped.
The application MUST have exactly one authoritative session persistence representation for AUTH-002.
A framework-native session representation MAY satisfy ENT-SESSION only if every canonical field and required invariant is concretely mapped and verified.
A custom session persistence representation MAY be introduced only after proving that the canonical contract cannot be satisfied by the native representation without semantic loss.
No duplicate session table or parallel session cache may become an alternate authorization authority.
Payload's generated authentication fields MUST remain distinct from the canonical Session contract unless an explicit field-level mapping proves equivalence.
Raw access tokens, refresh tokens and password material remain forbidden in any admitted Session persistence path.

decisionGate.step1: Inspect actual generated D1 schema for the auth-enabled Users collection and its sessions-related persistence.
decisionGate.step2: Inspect the Payload runtime auth/session implementation used by the installed version.
decisionGate.step3: Map native persistence fields and runtime semantics against all ENT-SESSION field IDs and invariants.
decisionGate.step4: If complete equivalence is proven, bind ENT-SESSION to the native representation and avoid duplicate persistence.
decisionGate.step5: If equivalence is not proven, keep native auth behavior as non-authoritative for the canonical contract and design the smallest explicit integration boundary required.

prohibitedInference: Assuming a field named sessions has the same semantics as ENT-SESSION.
Assuming a Payload JWT automatically provides canonical session revocation semantics.
Assuming refresh rotation semantics from documentation without runtime evidence.
Assuming a Payload-generated table name or column name without schema evidence.
Declaring ENT-SESSION VERIFIED merely because auth: true is configured.
requiredEvidenceBeforeImplementation: Payload-generated migration artifact containing the authentication/session schema
runtime source/version evidence for session issue, validation, refresh and logout
integration tests covering revoke, expiry and refresh replay
